title: LENGTH
definition: Returns the length of a string

title: UPPER
definition: UPPER(): Converts a string to uppercase.

title: LOWER
definition: LOWER(): Converts a string to lowercase.

title: LEFT
definition: In SQL, the LEFT() function returns the desired number of characters from the first characters of a string. This function will voluntarily truncate the input text to the desired length.

title: RIGHT
definition: In SQL language, the RIGHT() function allows you to extract the end of a string by defining the desired length. The function allows you to truncate a string starting from the end, by the desired number of characters.

title: SUBSTRING
definition: SUBSTRING(): Extracts a substring from a string.

title: REPLACE
column: replace(Just A Rather Very Small System,Small,Intelligent):basic_replace
definition:
Replaces a specified substring within a column with another value.
The function searches the column for the given text and substitutes it with the replacement text.
This is useful for cleaning or standardizing string values directly in a query.

Example: in the PRODUCTS_TABLE, the UNIT column may contain values such as '12 bottles'. Using unit.replace(bottles,bags) replaces the word bottles with bags, producing values like '12 bags'.

title: REVERSE
definition:
Reverses the characters of a string value.
The function returns the text in the opposite order from the original value.
For example: 'Chai' becomes 'iahC'.

title: TRIM
definition: In SQL language, the TRIM() function allows you to remove characters at the beginning and end of a string. Most often, the TRIM() function allows you to remove invisible characters, i.e. characters such as space, tab, line break or even carriage return. Such a function can be useful to save space in a database or to display data properly.

title: LTRIM
definition: In SQL, the LTRIM() function is used to remove characters from the beginning of a string. The most common use of LTRIM() is to remove invisible characters such as spaces, tabs, and newlines.

title: RTRIM
definition: In SQL, the RTRIM() function is used to remove characters from the end of a string. The most common use of RTRIM() is to remove invisible characters such as spaces, tabs, and newlines.

title: LPAD
definition:
Pads a string on the left side to a specified length.
The function adds the given character to the beginning of the value until the desired length is reached.
If the original string is longer than the specified length, it is truncated.

Example: lpad('Chai', 10, '*') → '******Chai'

title: RPAD
definition:
Pads a string on the right side to a specified length.
The function adds the given character to the end of the value until the desired length is reached.
If the original string is longer than the specified length, it is truncated.

Example: rpad('Chai', 10, '*') → 'Chai******'
